session.title: Who Owns the Exception?
session.bookReader: A general reader interested in how organisations make consequential decisions with AI

assumedKnowledge.book: No prior knowledge of organisation design, HR policy, or AI decision systems
assumedKnowledge.teaching: Familiarity with organisational decisions; specialist terms are introduced in the session

session.centralQuestion: Who may override an AI-supported recommendation when the case does not fit the rule?
session.nextQuestion: Which rules should remain fixed, which should be local, and which should be revised?

semanticBlocks.text: A recommendation crosses the policy threshold, the employee case does not fit the rule, and the workflow names no person who may authorize a departure.
A return-to-work recommendation flags an unusual employee case, but the workflow names no override owner or appeal route.
semanticBlocks.decision: Whether to follow, pause, or override the recommendation in this case
semanticBlocks.stakes: A wrong move can deny a defensible exception or make policy arbitrary
semanticBlocks.constraint: The ordinary rule does not fit and the workflow names no override route
semanticBlocks.incompleteEvidence: The recommendation does not contain all local context or the employee's correction
semanticBlocks.evidenceBoundary: The case is an illustrative composite, not a reported organisation

returnPoints.purpose: Re-read the case as an authority problem rather than a model-accuracy problem
returnPoints.newCausalWork: Shows why evidence can be adequate while the right to depart remains undefined

returnPoints.purpose: Trace how the recommendation reaches an authorised and appealable action
returnPoints.newCausalWork: Makes the missing override owner and challenge route operationally visible

semanticBlocks.text: An exception exposes who actually has authority when evidence and policy point in different directions.
In a synthetic port drill, the ordinary berth-allocation rule works until a damaged vessel blocks the channel and an exception owner must be named.
semanticBlocks.conceptualJob: Show that an exception exposes authority even outside employment decisions
semanticBlocks.mechanism: A blocked channel makes the ordinary allocation rule unusable until an exception owner acts
semanticBlocks.boundary: The port drill has no employment-rights or personal-fairness consequence
semanticBlocks.returnToHumanProblem: The comparison returns to the need to name who may depart from a rule and who can challenge that departure

semanticBlocks.text: Signal to recommendation to exception to authorized action to appeal and feedback.
Participants name the exception trigger, override owner, evidence requirement, and appeal route before AI responds.
AI questions ambiguous triggers, missing evidence, and absent appeal rights without choosing the decision.
Participants revise one line of the authority map and record why the change is defensible.
Map the rule, exception trigger, override owner, required evidence, explanation duty, and appeal path.
The next session asks where each rule should live and who may revise it.
semanticBlocks.unresolvedBecause: The session can define who may override without yet deciding where every rule should live
semanticBlocks.artifactState: The Exception Authority Map contains one unresolved rule-placement question

sceneToConcept.bridge: The case cannot move because a recommendation exists but no legitimate right to depart from it has been assigned
sceneToConcept.unresolvedConsequence: More evidence cannot settle a decision whose exception authority remains unnamed
sceneToConcept.nextMove: The next claim gives that missing organisational right a plain and usable name

conceptToFramework.bridge: Once the authority gap is visible, the full path from signal to appeal can be traced
conceptToFramework.unresolvedConsequence: Naming the authority gap still does not show how a recommendation becomes an appealable action
conceptToFramework.nextMove: The mechanism traces each handoff needed to turn the recommendation into accountable work

chapterToExercise.bridge: The reader must now decide how the missing right, evidence, action, and challenge route would be written
chapterToExercise.unresolvedConsequence: The path remains an explanation until somebody writes a bounded decision that another person can execute and challenge
chapterToExercise.nextMove: The exercise asks the learner to make that decision before seeing its hidden consequence

terms.plainDefinition: the bounded right to depart from an ordinary rule when a case meets stated conditions
terms.nearestDistinction: not the same as permission to ignore the rule whenever a manager disagrees

comparisonAudit.noComparisonNeededReason: This schema fixture teaches one authority mechanism; the port drill transfers the mechanism without comparing two evidence paths

book.centralQuestion: Who may override an AI-supported recommendation when the case does not fit the rule?
headings: The Case the Rule Did Not Expect
An Exception Is an Authority Test

visuals.visualJob: Show where evidence, authority, action, appeal, and feedback connect
visuals.proseRemoved: A repeated sentence-by-sentence recitation of the path

teaching.centralQuestion: Who may override an AI-supported recommendation when the case does not fit the rule?

coreSegments.facilitatorMove: Read the exception case aloud and stop before naming the missing design element.
coreSegments.participantMove: Choose whether to follow, pause, or override the recommendation and record one reason.
coreSegments.artifactState: The map contains a visible first decision before any framework appears.
coreSegments.recoveryMove: If the room debates model accuracy, return to the unnamed right to act.

coreSegments.facilitatorMove: Contrast an inaccurate recommendation with an accurate recommendation that nobody may override.
coreSegments.participantMove: Identify which difficulty belongs to evidence and which belongs to authority.
coreSegments.artifactState: The map separates recommendation quality from the right to depart from policy.
coreSegments.recoveryMove: If the distinction remains fuzzy, test it against the blocked-channel example.

coreSegments.facilitatorMove: Build the exception path one handoff at a time from evidence to challenge.
coreSegments.participantMove: Mark the first handoff in the case that lacks a named owner or rule.
coreSegments.artifactState: The map shows a specific break rather than a generic governance concern.
coreSegments.recoveryMove: If participants jump to solutions, ask which preceding handoff makes that solution legitimate.

coreSegments.facilitatorMove: Open the workbook at one decision fork and keep the consequence hidden.
coreSegments.participantMove: Write a first commitment and the consequence they knowingly accept.
coreSegments.artifactState: Every learner has a traceable choice that can survive later comparison.
coreSegments.recoveryMove: If choices stay abstract, require one actor, one action, and one accepted cost.

coreSegments.facilitatorMove: Reveal the bounded challenge and model questions that test missing evidence and rights.
coreSegments.participantMove: Use the challenge to locate one ambiguity without delegating the choice to AI.
coreSegments.artifactState: The map records one challenged assumption beside the learner's original commitment.
coreSegments.recoveryMove: If AI begins drafting the answer, reset it to questions and competing explanations.

coreSegments.facilitatorMove: Ask which part of the original commitment changes and which remains human-owned.
coreSegments.participantMove: Revise or retain one line and write the evidence for that decision.
coreSegments.artifactState: The map preserves both the first commitment and the reasoned revision.
coreSegments.recoveryMove: If everyone changes automatically, ask what evidence would justify keeping the first choice.

coreSegments.facilitatorMove: Reveal one completed edition only after all required fields contain meaningful attempts.
coreSegments.participantMove: Compare the two artifacts field by field and mark one defensible difference.
coreSegments.artifactState: The learner's version remains visible beside a realistic worked comparison.
coreSegments.recoveryMove: If the worked edition becomes an answer key, surface two alternative defensible boundaries.

coreSegments.facilitatorMove: Close on the unresolved question of where the ordinary and exception rules should live.
coreSegments.participantMove: Carry one unresolved rule-placement question forward on the completed map.
coreSegments.artifactState: The map is usable now and still contains the next design decision.
coreSegments.recoveryMove: If the room seeks closure, distinguish a usable artifact from a finished organisation design.

depthReserves.trigger: The room reaches the first map early or treats every exception as discretionary.
depthReserves.addedMove: Pairs write one observable exception trigger and one disconfirming condition.
depthReserves.participantMove: Each pair tests whether another person could apply the trigger without private context.
depthReserves.rejoin: Return to the case when every pair has one observable exception trigger.
depthReserves.artifactState: The Exception Authority Map has a testable trigger.

depthReserves.trigger: Most maps name an approver but no route for challenge.
depthReserves.addedMove: Pairs test who may contest the evidence and who can pause the action.
depthReserves.participantMove: Each pair adds one challenge route and the condition that pauses execution.
depthReserves.rejoin: Return at the completed appeal path before the filled-edition reveal.
depthReserves.artifactState: The map names an appeal owner and pause condition.

depthReserves.trigger: The filled-edition comparison ends with at least ten minutes available.
depthReserves.addedMove: Groups compare central, local, and split authority arrangements using the same exception.
depthReserves.participantMove: Each group selects one arrangement and names the consequence it accepts.
depthReserves.rejoin: Return with one rule-placement question for the next session.
depthReserves.artifactState: The map carries one unresolved rule-placement question.

exercises.name: Exception Authority Map

chapterConnection.unresolvedConsequence: The recommendation still cannot move legitimately because the chapter has exposed an exception path without assigning its concrete boundaries.
chapterConnection.firstParticipantAction: The learner must choose an immediate course of action and state the consequence that choice accepts.
chapterConnection.mechanismUsed: Each workbook field turns one handoff in the exception path into a named and challengeable commitment.

decisionFork.question: What should happen now that the ordinary rule does not fit and no exception owner is named?

options.action: Apply the ordinary recommendation without delay.
options.acceptedConsequence: Consistency is protected while relevant local context may remain unheard.

options.action: Pause the recommendation while gathering discriminating evidence.
options.acceptedConsequence: The decision slows while the organisation tests whether the case is materially different.

options.action: Authorise a time-bound exception with a review condition.
options.acceptedConsequence: Local context can change the outcome while inconsistency and precedent must be managed.

steps.prompt: Choose follow, pause, or bounded exception and state the consequence you accept.
After the hidden consequence appears, retain or revise the first choice and name the alternative now in view.
steps.output: A visible revision tied to the newly revealed consequence

steps.prompt: Name the live alternative and the evidence that could discriminate between the two accounts.
steps.output: An evidence test rather than a request for more information

steps.prompt: Name who may authorise the departure, who must be consulted, and who may challenge it.
steps.output: A bounded authority and challenge route

steps.prompt: Write the actor, action, and timing that make the commitment executable.
After the AI challenge, revise or retain the map and state the observation that would change it later.
steps.output: A reasoned revision and review condition

consequenceReveal.revealedFact: The source record omits an employee correction that would place the case outside the ordinary recommendation's stated boundary.
consequenceReveal.provenance: Illustrative fact introduced by the synthetic case designer rather than a claim about a named organisation.
consequenceReveal.decisionConsequence: The learner must now decide whether the omission changes the action or only changes the explanation required.

exercises.aiRole: Challenge the map by questioning ambiguous triggers, missing evidence, and absent appeal rights.
exercises.humanDecisionOwner: The named organizational role accountable for the affected people decision
exercises.transferPrompt: Apply the same six fields to one rule-bound decision in your own organisation using synthetic or redacted facts.
exercises.debriefQuestion: Which part of the path changed after challenge, and which right must still remain human-owned?

fields.answer: Pause automatic application of the ordinary rule for this case and open a seven-day bounded exception review; accept slower closure in exchange for a contestable decision.
The recommendation may be correct and the case may simply be inconvenient; the competing account is that material local context is absent from the record.
Compare the source evidence used by the recommendation with the employee's correction and two genuinely comparable prior cases; identify which omitted fact would change eligibility.

The policy owner defines the exception boundary, the line manager supplies local evidence, the CHRO's delegate authorises a time-bound departure, and the employee may challenge an omitted or incorrect fact within seven days.
The case owner pauses the automated recommendation today, records the reason, obtains the named evidence within five working days, and sends the authorised outcome with an explanation on day seven.
The policy owner reviews all exceptions after thirty days; two comparable upheld challenges or an error rate above five per cent triggers revision of the ordinary rule.

completeness.actors: Employee, line manager, case owner, policy owner, and CHRO delegate are named.
completeness.liveAlternative: The recommendation may be correct versus material local context may be missing.
completeness.evidenceDiscriminator: Source evidence, employee correction, and comparable prior cases can separate the accounts.
completeness.authorityBoundary: A time-bound exception is authorised by the CHRO delegate within a policy-owner boundary and remains challengeable.
completeness.executableAction: The case owner pauses today, gathers evidence within five days, and communicates an explained outcome on day seven.
completeness.revisionCondition: Thirty-day review with two upheld challenges or error above five per cent as the rule-change trigger.
completeness.appealOrChallengeRoute: The employee can challenge an omitted or incorrect fact within seven days.
